- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 75+), then sharply correct downward — model fails to capture this “rebound” or “mean reversion” effect.
- Model exhibits persistent downward bias in the latter half of the forecast (days 20–30), often underestimating true values by 1–3 points.
- Model reacts too slowly to recent price drops — fails to adjust forecast downward when recent history shows falling prices.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility — underestimates short-term price swings, especially downward corrections.
- Forecasts often lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, particularly in the first 10 days.
- Model overreacts to recent high prices — forecasts remain elevated even after prices drop, suggesting poor “memory decay” or “forgetting” of recent trends.
- Model underestimates the impact of recent low prices — fails to recognize that a low price may trigger a rebound, leading to underestimation of future values.
- Model shows strong bias toward higher prices in the first 5 days, then gradually adjusts — suggests a “warm-up” or “initial overconfidence” bias.
- Model does not adequately account for seasonal or cyclical patterns — e.g., price tends to dip in late July, but model often fails to predict this.
